Degree-preserving edge-swap null for co-expressolog statistics

Source: R/coexpressolog_null.R
coexpressolog_null.Rd

Tests whether an observed co-expressolog statistic exceeds what network topology alone produces. Each species network is binarised at its analysis threshold and rewired by degree-preserving edge swaps (igraph::keeping_degseq()), which keeps every gene's degree but destroys the correspondence between network neighbourhoods and the ortholog mapping. find_coexpressologs then runs on the rewired networks with exactly the same arguments (...) as the observed run, and the statistic is compared against the resulting null distribution.

coexpressolog_null(
  networks,
  orthologs,
  statistic = NULL,
  n_perm = 100L,
  swap_factor = 10L,
  n_cores = 1L,
  seed = 1L,
  ...
)

Arguments

networks

Named list of sparse network objects (compute_network(sparse = TRUE) outputs), keyed by species abbreviation. Dense networks are rejected; convert them with as_sparse_network.

orthologs

Data frame with columns Species1, Species2, hog, as for find_coexpressologs.

statistic

Function mapping the find_coexpressologs() edge data frame to a named numeric vector, or NULL (default) for the count of rows with type == "conserved" per species pair (named paste(species1, species2, sep = "~")) plus "total". For the built-in statistic, a null run whose rewiring leaves a species pair with no overlap > 0 rows records 0 conserved calls for that pair; a user-supplied statistic missing a name from the observed run errors.

n_perm

Number of rewired permutations (default 100).

swap_factor

Edge swaps per permutation, as a multiple of the edge count of each thresholded network (default 10).

n_cores

Number of parallel workers for the permutation loop (default 1).

seed

Integer base seed; worker b uses seed + b (default 1).

...

Passed unchanged to find_coexpressologs for both the observed and every null run (species_pairs, method, alternative, alpha, pval_combine, pi0_method, ...).

Value

Data frame with one row per statistic and columns statistic, observed, null_mean, null_sd, null_max, fold (observed / null_mean; NA when the null mean is 0) and p_emp ((1 + sum(null >= observed)) / (n_perm + 1)). The n_perm x k matrix of null statistics is attached as attr(, "null").

Details

Rewiring operates on the network thresholded at net$threshold (the analysis density), not on the stored superset: sparse-store entries with values at or above the threshold become edges, the rest are dropped. The rewired networks are unweighted (every stored value is 1, with threshold = 1 and store_threshold = 1), so only membership-based consumers are valid downstream; edge weights carry no information after rewiring. Each network is rewired with swap_factor * igraph::ecount(g) swaps and stays simple (no loops, no multi-edges).

Permutation b runs in a worker that calls set.seed(seed + b) first, so results are reproducible and independent of n_cores. On Unix the permutations run under parallel::mclapply(); on Windows they run serially. The serial path saves and restores the caller's RNG state around the loop, so the ambient stream continues where the observed run left it. The observed run uses the ambient RNG: call set.seed() beforehand when ... includes settings that draw from it (e.g. the default pi0_method = "randomized"). method = "permutation" in ... is allowed but slow (a full permutation test per rewired network).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
set.seed(1)
res <- coexpressolog_null(networks, orthologs, n_perm = 100L,
                          n_cores = 4L)
res[res$statistic == "total", ]
} # }
